# 3.4 LIS in O(n log n), LCS, edit distance

Phase 3 (Recursion to dynamic programming), target rating 1500–1900. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### Longest increasing subsequence (`lis`)

Length of the longest strictly (or non-strictly) increasing subsequence in O(n log n) with the "smallest tail" array.

**Works because:** The smallest-tail array is sorted, so the position to update is found by searching.

### Problems that reduce to it (`lis-reduction`)

After sorting by one key, the question becomes the longest increasing chain in the other key (nested boxes, envelopes, chains of pairs).

**Works because:** Sorting by the first key (with the right tie order) leaves exactly the second-key increasing condition.

### Longest common subsequence (`lcs`)

Length or one example of the longest common subsequence of two sequences in O(n·m).

**Works because:** n · m fits the budget, and the answer for two prefixes depends only on shorter prefixes.

### Edit distance (`edit-distance`)

Minimum insertions, deletions, and replacements to turn one string into another.

**Works because:** Every edit sequence can be reordered to act on the strings from left to right, so the state is a pair of prefixes.
